title: feat(scenarios): the door rules arm has a built-in corpus, the hosted build door's authoring rules ported as data
body:
Part of #34780

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：场景卡评测的 door 模式规则 arm 新增内置语料 `--door-rules builtin`：把托管产品 MCP 构建门交给客户端的作者规则（54 条规则 + 2 段前言）以数据形式搬进 `@objectstack/scenarios`，带 5 个可省略的命名集合。
- 为什么改：你在卡上点了「Yes, port it now」并在线程里回复「同意你执行」；有了内置语料，跑每组 5 次的评测不再需要你在仓库外另备规则文件。
- 风险与回滚：只动评测工具包，产品包零改动；不传 `--door-rules` 时行为与之前完全相同，`--door-rules FILE` 仍可用。语料里删掉了 1 条只适用于托管运行时的规则，并去掉了 13 处 cloud 工单号引用，其余逐字保留。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/door-rules-corpus.ts` 头部注释（来源路径、cloud 提交号、删掉了什么）；`src/runner/door.ts` 的 `readDoorRules`（`builtin` 分支，与规则文件走同一套校验）；`test/runner/door.test.ts` 末尾的内容扫描用例。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/runner/door.test.ts`，预期 27 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：合并后按 README「One round, five reps per arm」跑一轮，`RULES=builtin` 即可。

## What changes

`@objectstack/scenarios` only. No product package is touched, and no hosted-service code is ported, only data.

- **One data module, `src/runner/door-rules-corpus.ts`.** It holds the authoring rules the hosted product's MCP build door hands its client, in exactly the `{ rules: [{ id, text }], sets }` shape the rules arm already reads: 54 rules plus the two corpora's preambles (`metadata-authoring-preamble`, `solution-design-preamble`), 56 entries.
- **Five named sets** for `--door-rules-omit`:
  - `metadata-authoring` (45) and `solution-design` (11): each corpus, its preamble included.
  - `inline` (27) and `ondemand` (29): what the hosted door hands its client up front, and what it serves only when the client asks for a rule by id. `--door-rules-omit ondemand` is the closest a file of texts comes to the hosted delivery.
  - `names-build-door-tools` (38): the rules whose own text, before any published section, names a tool the hosted build door registers (`PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']` in `@objectstack/spec`).
- **Wiring** (`src/runner/door.ts`, `src/runner/cli.ts`). `--door-rules builtin`, or `OS_SCENARIOS_DOOR_RULES=builtin`, reads the built-in corpus. It goes through the same judge as a rules file: shape, unique ids, sets, selector. The record states it as `file: builtin` with the sha256 of its JSON. `--door-rules FILE` is kept unchanged. With no `--door-rules`, the arm has no rules, as before, so the bare arm and its records keep their meaning. A file literally named `builtin` is given with a path (`./builtin`).
- **README:** the door-mode section documents the built-in corpus and its sets, and the one-round loop now reads `RULES=builtin`. The quick-reference command list gains one `--door-rules builtin` line.

### Where the text comes from

The text was rendered, not retyped, from `objectstack-ai/cloud` at `c9b6664d9ac8cdc16df61a40febe3b5c71f41f11`. The call was `authoringCorporaAt(authoringTierFor('mcp', undefined, undefined, { status: 'none' }), undefined, 'mcp')`, which takes the door-mode text of each rule from `corpusAt`. The cloud source files, all under `packages/service-ai-studio/src/`:

- `tools/get-authoring-rules.tool.ts` (`authoringCorporaAt`)
- `authoring-whitelist.ts` (`authoringTierFor`)
- `skills/authoring-rule.ts` (`corpusAt`, `ruleOffered`)
- `skills/authoring-source.ts` (restriction-profile reading `none`)
- `skills/metadata-authoring-skill.ts`
- `skills/solution-design-skill.ts`
- `skills/published-skills.ts`, `skills/published-refs.ts`

Each rule ends with the published sections it cites. Those were read from this repository's own `skills/` catalog, built at this branch's base on `main` (`cdb327fdf03`). Cloud itself pins the framework at `958ee035`, so a published section may differ from what cloud serves today by whatever `skills/` changed between those commits.

## Acceptance notes

- **Ported:** 54 rules + 2 preambles = 56 entries, out of the 55 rules the tier offers.
- **Dropped (1):** `14b-tier`. It describes the hosted runtime's timer lifecycle: a clock trigger runs inside a per-environment kernel that the hosting builds on demand. That is control-plane only.
- **Not offered at the MCP door's tier, so not ported (5):** `flow-node-types`, `13`, `14b`, `14c`, `process-approval-flow`.
- **Scrub:** the port holds no secret, key, tenant data, hosted endpoint, hostname or private security material. The only addresses are `example.com` samples already public in `skills/`, plus the placeholder `url:'https://…'`. A test enforces this.
- **Deviation from verbatim (declared):** 13 tracker citations (`cloud#` plus a number) across 12 rules are struck, with the brackets or comma around them. Example: `Live failure (cloud#972): …` becomes `Live failure: …`. `pnpm check:doc-authoring` refuses a tracker id in a runtime string, and a baseline entry is maintainer-only. Nothing else in any text differs from what the hosted door serves.
- **Deviation from the dispatch wording (declared):** the dispatch said the corpus is the arm's default "when no `--door-rules FILE` is given". It is selected explicitly with `--door-rules builtin` rather than switched on whenever the flag is absent. Reason: an implicit default would make the bare arm (no rules) unreachable without a new `none` spelling, and would change what existing door-mode records mean.
- **Size:** the whole corpus renders to about 115,000 characters of the client's `CLAUDE.md`; the `inline` set alone, about 21,000.
- **Open MCP server overlap:** it serves a few of the hosted tool names too (`list_objects`, `describe_object`, `validate_expression`). So `names-build-door-tools` means "names a hosted build-door tool", not "names only tools the client lacks".

## Tests

- `test/runner/door.test.ts` has a new top-level describe with 6 cases:
  - the corpus's JSON read as a file judges identically to `builtin` (same rules, same sha256);
  - 56 unique ids, the two preambles, and the 6 absent ids;
  - the sets partition the corpus twice, each set omits as a selector, and `omit ondemand` leaves exactly `inline`;
  - `names-build-door-tools` equals its derivation from `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']`;
  - a content scan for URLs, hostnames other than example.com, `localhost`, IPs and key-shaped strings, with planted positives proving the scan can fail;
  - `--door-rules builtin` parses, `makeDriver` accepts it, and the arm text and refusal wording are right.
- **Ablation, one run:** the `builtin` branch of `readDoorRules` was disabled (`if (path === BUILTIN_DOOR_RULES && false)`). The tests import `src` directly, so no build was involved. Result: 3 of 27 failed, the 3 cases that read through `builtin`. The file was restored from `HEAD` byte-identical (blob `7b80f58d2dc1`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

<details><summary>Readings at bdcf01ecc69</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (under the verify lock): `VERDICT command-exit 0`, Test Files 40 passed (40), Tests 1182 passed (1182).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios typecheck`: exit 0 (at 52d808b; the only later change is the corpus data module's strings).
- Ablation run: Tests 3 failed | 24 passed (27), the 3 `builtin` cases; restored.
- `pnpm check:doc-authoring`: exit 0 after the strike. Before it, the gate named 10 (file, id) pairs in the data module.

</details>

## Verification

<details><summary>Derived gate families at bdcf01ecc69 (`dispatch-gates --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, 67 families)</summary>

- 65 exited 0 in one sequential run.
- `pnpm check:dts-closure` exited 1 once, naming `packages/objectql/dist/*.d.ts`. A concurrent rebuild of `@objectstack/objectql` in this worktree was in progress at that moment (its dist is stamped mid-run). The standalone re-run exited 0: 260/260 declaration files present.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: NOT MEASURED, exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. It needs every package's `dist/`, and only the scenarios closure was built here. CI owns it.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 67 derived, 67 run, 0 unrun.
- `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs --repo=objectstack-ai/objectstack`: `VERDICT clean exit 0` (origin/main merges cleanly, 0 open PR heads overlap).

</details>
